name: rea
description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
one_liner: Gives an AI assistant the tools to pull apart how an app or program actually works under the hood, down to the raw binary, instead of a human doing it by hand.
buyer: A security consultant or legacy-software contractor who gets paid to figure out how an undocumented app, device driver, or old binary works before they can fix, clone, or audit it.
business_use_cases: A security firm uses it to speed up malware and vulnerability triage, cutting the hours billed per engagement.
A contractor hired to maintain a 15-year-old program with no source code uses it to reconstruct how key features work before touching the code.
A compatibility-layer vendor uses it to understand undocumented native libraries they need to re-implement.

money_ideas.idea: Offer reverse-engineering-as-a-service for legacy software audits, pricing by engagement.
Package it with prebuilt analysis playbooks for specific binary formats and sell to security teams.

steal_this: A paid 'legacy app autopsy' service: point this at an old undocumented .exe or firmware dump and sell the client a readable report of what it actually does.
